guard: a turn Claude Code ended on StopFailure is published as a run error carrying the harness's own error kind, and a turn that ended on Stop is not
why: CELLS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN, not chosen from the wreckage afterwards.
C1 is the state this connector shipped in: `Stop` and `StopFailure` shared one arm and one
close, so a turn killed by a rate limit or a billing error was published as a turn that
finished. It is the mutation that reproduces the defect, and the cell it reddens is the one that
C2 is the OPPOSITE failure, and it is the one worth guarding hardest, because the two hooks
already shared an arm: widening the predicate by one character turns every normal turn end into
a published failure. Without C2 the suite could not tell a mapping from a blanket, and a blanket
would pass every failure cell in the file.
C3 is the reason. The harness names one of eleven error kinds and that name is the whole of what
a consumer can act on; a RUN_ERROR with no code says the turn failed and refuses to say how.
NOT REGISTERED, and named rather than left as a hole: nothing mutates the flush that runs before
the close. Its property — that the turn's records are on the wire before the terminal that ends
them — belongs to the arm both hooks already shared and is not what this change touches.
